a4_repro.cause: Joblib reload reproduced the in-memory scores exactly, including the Stage 7 checkpoint. RunResult.to_dict had stored round(threshold, 6). That moved the validation threshold from the exact quantile-grid value onto 6e-6. One negative test claim scored between those two cuts, so precision and F1 changed and AUROC did not. The discrepancy is threshold serialization, not model serialization, prediction drift, or a second fit.

1_stage7_confounded.statement: Yes. Stage 7 set the model seed equal to the split seed, so each reported seed changed the question assignment and, for models that read that seed, the initialization together. The two generators were already separate. The confounding is in that coupled design, not in a hidden shared stream.

2_variance_attribution.statement: At a fixed model seed, A7's AUROC SD across the 20 splits is 0.0600, 0.1509, and 0.0883. The median within-split SD is 0.1169 and the maximum is 0.2068. Both the split and the model seed move A7. With three model seeds, the initialization term is preliminary. The method-of-moments between-split share is undefined, on repeated partitions of one pool.

3_unstable_at_fixed_initialization.criterion: AUROC range across the 20 splits exceeds 0.10 at that fixed model seed
3_unstable_at_fixed_initialization.statement: Yes. With the model seed held fixed, A7's test AUROC still spans 0.2009 at model seed 0, 0.4911 at model seed 1, 0.3745 at model seed 2. The criterion is a range above 0.10. Initialization is not required for that movement.

4_unstable_at_fixed_split.statement: Within a split, A7's AUROC SD across the three model seeds has median 0.1169, minimum 0.0474, and maximum 0.2068. Initialization still moves A7 when the split is held fixed. Three model seeds make this a preliminary description, not a precise population SD.

A0.statement: No stable advantage over A0. The split-level mean delta is positive on 6 of 20 splits and negative on 14. Of 60 separate paired intervals, 3 lie entirely above 0 and 9 lie entirely below 0. Interval endpoints are not averaged.

A4.statement: No stable advantage over A4. The split-level mean delta is positive on 4 of 20 splits and negative on 16. Of 60 separate paired intervals, 2 lie entirely above 0 and 14 lie entirely below 0. Interval endpoints are not averaged.

6_a4_checkpoint.cause: Joblib reload reproduced the in-memory scores exactly, including the Stage 7 checkpoint. RunResult.to_dict had stored round(threshold, 6). That moved the validation threshold from the exact quantile-grid value onto 6e-6. One negative test claim scored between those two cuts, so precision and F1 changed and AUROC did not. The discrepancy is threshold serialization, not model serialization, prediction drift, or a second fit.

7_metrics_reconstructed.statement: Yes. All 480 reported point-metric blocks were recomputed from the saved validation scores, the saved test scores, and a second load of the checkpoint.
